senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; יָכַח)reproof, admonition, threat of punishment.
units: <cite ref="Arakhin 16b:40">Arakh. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>תמיהני</he> … <he>שמקבל ת׳</he> I wonder whether in this generation there is one that accepts admonition; Sifra K’dosch., Par. 2, ch. IV. Arakh. l. c. <he>עד היכן ת׳ וכ׳</he> how far must you go in reproving your neighbor (<cite ref="Leviticus 19:17">Lev. XIX, 17</cite>)? Until he strikes you.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 27:6">Lev. R. s. 27</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 1:18">Is. I, 18</cite>) <he>זו תשובה וזו ת׳</he> is this an argument, and this a threat?; Tanḥ. Emor 10; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 554:2">Yalk. Mic. 554</cite>.

<cite ref="Chagigah 4b:8">Ḥag. 4ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 45:3">Gen. XLV, 3</cite>) <he>ומה ת׳ של בשר ודם כך ת׳ וכ׳</he> if the rebuke of a human being has such an effect, how much greater ought to be the effect of God’s rebuke!; a. fr.—Pl. <he>תּוֹכָחוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Tamid 28a:11">Tam. 28ᵃ</cite> <he>יאהב את הת׳ שכל זמן שת׳ וכ׳</he> let man love reproofs, for as long as reproofs are in the world, ease of mind comes upon the world, good, and blessing &c.

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 1:13">Deut. R. s. 1</cite> <he>ראויין היו הת׳ וכ׳</he> the rebukes (threats of punishment) should have been pronounced through Balaam, and the blessings through Moses; <cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 1:9">ib.</cite> <he>יוכיחן משה … והת׳ ביד ישראל</he> let Moses who loves them rebuke them, and Balaam who hates them, bless them in order that the blessings and the rebukes be made certain in Israel’s hand; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 795:1">Yalk. ib. 795</cite>. Deut. R. l. c. <he>הואיל וקבלו עליהן תּוֹכְחוֹתֶיךָ וכ׳</he> because they accepted thy (Moses’) rebukes, thou must bless them; a. fr.
